title: All-section and transport comparisons over an inner-horn completion
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor categories and coherent natural equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the smallness convention of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and cocartesian fibrations over arbitrary simplicial bases and marked inverse equivalences as in [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. Fix an uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa$. Let $i:X\hookrightarrow X'$ be a monomorphism of $\kappa$-small simplicial sets, with $X'$ a quasicategory, obtained as a countable composite of pushouts of coproducts of inner horn inclusions $\Lambda_j^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<j<n$. Let $q:Y\to X$ and $q':Y'\to X'$ be cocartesian fibrations, and suppose $u:Y\to i^*Y'$ over $X$ preserves cocartesian edges and has an inverse up to coherent natural equivalences over $X$, also preserving cocartesian edges. The total spaces may be arbitrarily large in a fixed containing universe. Write $\Gamma(q)_n=\{s:X\times\Delta^n\to Y\mid qs=\operatorname{pr}_X\}$, and similarly for the other fibrations.

The simplicial sets $\Gamma(q)$, $\Gamma(i^*q')$ and $\Gamma(q')$ are quasicategories. Postcomposition $u_*:\Gamma(q)\to\Gamma(i^*q')$ and restriction $i^*:\Gamma(q')\to\Gamma(i^*q')$ are functor equivalences; restriction has the right lifting property against every simplicial monomorphism in the containing universe. For every vertex $x\in X$, $u$ gives a fiber equivalence $u_x:Y_x\to Y'_{i(x)}$, and the identities $\operatorname{ev}_x u_*=u_x\operatorname{ev}_x$ and $\operatorname{ev}_x i^*=\operatorname{ev}_{i(x)}$ hold. Thus quasi-inverses give evaluation squares commuting up to coherent natural equivalence.

For every old edge $e:x\to z$, the fiber equivalences intertwine its transport functors up to coherent natural equivalence. Here transport along an edge means a functor on the initial fiber with a cylinder into the total space over that edge, restricting to the initial inclusion and the final fiber inclusion composed with the functor, whose vertex edges are cocartesian. Let $\mathcal J$ be any collection of quasicategorical indexing shapes in the containing universe. If every fiber of $q$ admits all $J$-indexed colimits for $J\in\mathcal J$ and every edge transport of $q$ preserves them, then every fiber of $q'$ admits these colimits and every edge transport of $q'$ preserves them. No filteredness of fibers or section categories is assumed or asserted.
